chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Safwan ibn Yahya from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

For the prayer, an angel is assigned who has no other work besides it. When he finishes with it, he gathers it and ascends with it. If it is among that which is accepted, it is accepted; and if it is among that which is not accepted, it is said to him: 'Return it to My servant.' So he descends with it until he strikes the servant's face with it, then he says to him: 'Exile/annoyance to you, your deed will continually trouble me.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the prayer if it is rejected by the angel?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the unique role of the angel assigned exclusively to prayer, illustrating the tangible spiritual consequences of neglecting its prime time. The imagery of the angel striking the worshipper’s face with the rejected prayer signifies a persistent, internalized disgrace that serves as a continuous reminder of the missed obligation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the physical and spiritual integrity of ritual acts, where the quality of performance directly impacts the soul's state.
